questions.q: Define crossing over and state the exact stage of prophase I when it occurs, naming the enzyme responsible.
questions.a: Crossing over is the reciprocal exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, occurring during pachytene stage of prophase I, mediated by the enzyme recombinase. A wrong answer (e.g., "occurs in metaphase I" or "involves sister chromatids") reveals confusion between homologous vs. sister chromatid interactions and misplacement of the event in the meiotic timeline.

questions.q: Explain why independent assortment of chromosomes during metaphase I generates genetic variation, but independent assortment of sister chromatids in metaphase II does not.
questions.a: In metaphase I, homologous chromosomes (each carrying different alleles) orient randomly at the equator, so maternal and paternal chromosomes segregate independently into gametes, creating new allele combinations. In metaphase II, sister chromatids are identical copies (barring crossing over), so their separation does not produce new combinations. A wrong answer indicates failure to distinguish between segregation of homologous chromosomes vs. sister chromatids and their allelic content.

questions.q: A diploid organism has 2n = 6 chromosomes. Calculate the number of genetically distinct gamete types possible from independent assortment alone, assuming no crossing over. Show your reasoning.
questions.a: Haploid number n = 3. Independent assortment yields 2ⁿ = 2³ = 8 distinct gamete combinations. Reasoning: each homologous pair segregates independently, giving 2 choices per pair; total combinations = product of choices = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. A wrong answer (e.g., 6 or 4) reveals misunderstanding of the 2ⁿ formula or confusion between chromosome number and haploid number.

questions.q: Compare the genetic composition of the four daughter cells produced by meiosis in a heterozygous individual (Aa) for a single gene, with and without crossing over between the gene locus and the centromere.
questions.a: Without crossing over: two cells get A, two get a (parental types only). With crossing over between locus and centromere: recombinant chromatids form, so all four cells can be genetically distinct (A, a, and two recombinants if multiple crossovers). A wrong answer (e.g., "always four different types") shows failure to link crossover position relative to centromere and gene locus to the segregation pattern in meiosis II.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Meiosis reduces chromosome number by half, so it decreases genetic diversity in the population." Justify your answer with two specific mechanisms.
questions.a: The statement is false. Although meiosis halves chromosome number, it increases genetic diversity via (1) crossing over — creating recombinant chromosomes with new allele combinations, and (2) independent assortment — shuffling maternal/paternal chromosomes randomly into gametes. Fertilization then combines two such varied gametes. A wrong evaluation indicates conflation of chromosome number reduction with loss of genetic information, ignoring the combinatorial explosion of allelic arrangements.

questions.q: Give the correct order of steps in a Drosophila test-cross that measures recombination between vestigial wings and black body.
questions.a: The cross runs: (1) Cross a homozygous wild-type fly with a double recessive vestigial black fly (2) Test-cross the heterozygous F1 to the double recessive (3) Score progeny as parental wild-type, vestigial black or recombinant classes (4) Compute the recombination frequency as recombinants over total times 100. A wrong answer that uses unlinked genes or omits the test-cross shows the student has missed that measurable recombination needs heterozygous alleles revealed against a homozygous recessive parent.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Meiosis is a ______ reductional cell division in diploid germ cells that produces four genetically unique haploid gametes through two sequential divisions (Meiosis I and II) following a single DNA replication, thereby halving the chromosome number and generating genetic variation via crossing over and independent assortment.
Fill in the blank: ______ a family photograph: siblings share parents but look different — different eye colour, height, hair texture.
What is Meiosis? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Meiosis is a specialized reductional cell division in diploid germ cells that produces four genetically unique haploid gametes through two sequential divisions (Meiosis I and II) following a single DNA replication, thereby halving the chromosome number and generating genetic variation via crossing over and independent assortment.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Meiosis?
questions.a: Students often think crossing over occurs between sister chromatids because they look identical, or that independent assortment happens in metaphase II because chromatids separate then.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can explain how crossing over at chiasmata during pachytene and random orientation of bivalents at metaphase I create recombinant chromosomes and independent assortment, and can calculate the number of possible gamete combinations (2ⁿ) for a given haploid number n.
